clue.text: There's many a shipwreck caused by accident

indicators.note: a wreck is something smashed up, so the letters before it are broken and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many
taken as written
the first four letters are the fodder; the rest of the word is the signal

explanation.surface: A rueful saying that plenty of maritime disasters happen purely by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipwreck' reads as one word, but it splits into the fodder ship and the signal wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky incident, a minor accident.

clue.text: Island forced to join a revolutionary organisation

parts.note: made, as in made someone do something
the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: An island population coerced into joining an insurgent group.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, west of Morocco.

clue.text: Having little science, a politician can appear a rogue

parts.note: SC is a short form of science, as in BSc
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A poorly educated member of parliament may come across as a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened word here rather than a small amount of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a playful kind of rogue.

clue.text: Preparing tea — sure to be quite plain

indicators.note: preparing something means making it up from ingredients, so the following letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making a pot of tea that is bound to be very ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severely simple and without decoration.

clue.text: Make up for disappointing spread

parts.note: an off performance is a disappointing one
to set things out is to spread or lay them out, as in setting a table

explanation.surface: Someone compensating for a meal or buffet that let the guests down.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance or compensate for it.

clue.text: Picture a man bound up with business

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom towards the top

parts.note: a serf was a man bound to his lord's land
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: An image of a man deeply involved in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound up with' reads as a single phrase meaning involved in; split it, and bound goes with the man while up turns him round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a picture painted on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: Outstanding swine coming to bad end, and that's right

parts.note: a star turn is an outstanding one
a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of bad

explanation.surface: A notable pig meets a sorry fate, and rightly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad end' reads as a grim fate, but it is just the last letter of bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: Job a character found in "Pickwick Papers"

definitions.text: Job a character found in "Pickwick Papers"

parts.note: surface reading: some task or a personality to be found in Dickens's novel; setter's reading: Job is the first name of a Pickwick Papers character, and the answer is his surname

explanation.surface: A literary question about a figure in Dickens's first novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Job looks like a common noun, a task, but it is a first name; the answer completes the name of the servant of the villain Jingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Job Trotter is Alfred Jingle's sly manservant in The Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Reason against the team taking a fixed amount

parts.note: as in pros and cons
a side is a team
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: An argument against the team being given a set allocation.
explanation.definitionFit: A consideration is a factor or reason weighed in coming to a decision.

clue.text: Fancy a little hide-away

indicators.note: a little of the following word means only part of its letters are taken, a run from inside it

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of hide across the hyphen into away

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a small secluded retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb of wanting, but it is a noun meaning a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim that comes into the mind, which is an idea.

clue.text: The craftsman's son's mate — no use

indicators.note: to use material is to work it into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad remark that a tradesman's son's friend is good for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after craftsman is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'no use' reads as a verdict, but use is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone, a classic craftsman.

clue.text: Not an exotic plant

parts.note: surface reading: an ordinary garden plant rather than a rare imported one; setter's reading: an old word for a medicinal herb, which is also the everyday word for plain or unfussy

explanation.surface: A gardener describing a homely native plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both the adjective for something plain, not exotic, and an old noun for a herb used in home remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is a herb gathered for medicine, and as an adjective it means plain, the opposite of exotic.

clue.text: Musical instruments still kept in bags

indicators.note: something kept in a holder sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: sacks are bags
still in the sense of nevertheless, yet

explanation.surface: Instruments that are still stored away in their carrying bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about the instruments resting, but it means however.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackbuts are early trombones, brass instruments of Renaissance music.

clue.text: Day-dream possibly about a point prepared

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters of the word before it may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, the hyphen ignored
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A dreamer's reverie built up around one point, ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepared has been got ready in advance.

clue.text: Cure no age problem but offer support

indicators.note: a problem is a muddle, so the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ageing cannot be cured, but you can still back someone through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone is to give them support and confidence.

clue.text: Look on the pound as an animal refuge

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece placed on another is written after it, so the first-named comes second

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Viewing the council dog pound as a shelter for strays.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the look follows the pound; 'pound' suggests an animal pound, but it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is the den where a wild animal shelters.

clue.text: Opt for a non-electric tool

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pointed hand tool for breaking hard ground

explanation.surface: Choosing a hand tool over a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one instruction, it is advice to buy manual; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to choose, and a pick is a hand-swung tool for breaking up earth or ice.

clue.text: A top journalist under strain

parts.note: surface reading: a senior reporter working under pressure; setter's reading: the editor of the newspaper world, the Press's ED, written as one word means being squeezed

explanation.surface: A senior journalist suffering under deadline stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: the Press (journalists as a body) followed by ED, the top journalist, makes a word meaning under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pressed, as in pressed for time, is under pressure or strain.

clue.text: Leading coppers falling back

parts.note: P stands for pence, and copper coins are pennies
receding means retreating or falling back

explanation.surface: The front-running police officers start to drop behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but it is copper coins; 'back' here is part of the phrase, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Preceding means going before, so leading in order or time.

clue.text: Visits give a boy a name!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pays a visit to
second meaning, split differently: to give a name to a male child

explanation.walkthrough: Read as call son, the answer means name a boy; read as a phrasal verb it means visits.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a short visit.

clue.text: Report a ranter broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item on a loudmouth's radio or television appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a radio term, but it signals the letters being scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or report a sequence of events.

clue.text: The staff pop back inside for a savoury morsel

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, as is pa

explanation.surface: Kitchen staff popping back in to fetch a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees and 'pop back' a quick return; both are false.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury bite served with drinks.

clue.text: Let up maybe before a worker gets cantankerous

indicators.note: maybe hints that the preceding letters are only one possible order and may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: An employee who becomes bad-tempered when told to ease off.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant means sulkily irritable, close to cantankerous in sense.

clue.text: Last railway uniform

parts.note: to last is to survive, to live on
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: The final uniform worn by railway staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective meaning final, but it is a verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or company staff.

clue.text: A girl in love's tactful

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the words that follow, running across the gap between them

parts.note: the run starts at the third letter of love's and ends at the second letter of tactful

explanation.surface: A young woman whose romance is handled with discretion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tactful' looks like the definition at the end, but it only holds the tail of the answer; the definition is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesta is a female first name, taken from the Roman goddess of the hearth.

clue.text: Up and down they go endlessly

definitions.text: Up and down they go endlessly

parts.words: Up and down they go endlessly
parts.note: surface reading: something restless, such as yo-yos or a fidgety person, bobbing about forever; setter's reading: moving staircases whose steps loop round without end, some carrying people up and some down

explanation.surface: Things that keep bobbing up and down without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving stairways run on a continuous loop of steps, rising or descending between floors.

clue.text: Backing friends, makes a hit

indicators.note: backing means moving in the rear direction, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Supporting one's friends turns out to be a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing friends' reads as loyalty and 'makes a hit' as succeeding; the hit is a literal blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To slap is to strike with the open hand, so it makes a hit.

clue.text: Become more intense as a letter writer

parts.note: the spelt-out name of the letter D
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone whose feelings grow stronger as they write letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter writer' suggests a correspondent, but it splits into a letter's name and a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours, feelings and crises are said to deepen when they grow stronger.

clue.text: Fed by the hotel, as is natural

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
fed in the sense of having eaten

explanation.surface: Guests being fed by their hotel, as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside: the eating word sits next to the hotel, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, natural rather than acquired.
